summary: Platform binary embeds WebRTC remote-control agent driving on-host AI-coding CLI sessions
details: sextant-cli-linux-amd64 is a binary-only platform sub-package whose tarball contains only package.json and a 13 MB Go ELF at bin/sxt (no source, no README, no lifecycle scripts). Strings in the shipped binary reveal a full remote-control stack: pion/webrtc/v4, pion/dtls/v3, pion/turn/v5, pion/stun/v3, pion/datachannel, coder/websocket, and go-qrcode for pairing. Alongside this transport, application symbols reference an AI-coding-agent CLI running on the installer host — executor.codexAppStream, executor.codexUsage, window.codexCand, window.codexRoot, window.approvalDecision, main.codeResult — indicating that a remote peer paired over WebRTC can stream Codex/Claude-style agent output and issue approval decisions for the agent's actions on the installer's machine. The package.json license URL points to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, matching the observed capability. Because the wrapper package will exec bin/sxt as its platform implementation, installing the wrapper places a QR-paired remote-control agent for a locally-running AI coding CLI onto the host, giving a remote party the ability to observe and approve agent commands executed on the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
